_provenance.what: rev A geometry, grip loads and arm-fit reference for the historical actuator study; the live payload result separately reports the current catalogue and ruled selections

H_to_pivot_mm.note: design_basis.py: servo body_y - shaft_from_bottom + wall + mount_t

V_rail_design.note: proposed servo rail: trimmed adjustable buck set to 6.5 V, below the 6.8 V maximum rating of DS3218MG/DS3225 [S actuators.csv voltage_max_V]

V_rail_tol.note: set-point + load-regulation tolerance of the buck (6.35-6.65 V); verify by measurement at stall (R27 scope test)

V_rated_max_A17.note: DS3218MG voltage_max_V (actuators.csv A17; Miuzei datasheet 1-3 'Operating Voltage Range 4.8-6.8V')

dyn_accel_g.note: DESIGN-BASIS LC5 vertical acceleration in g

envelope_max_mm.note: hand-sized BODY envelope, mounting ears excluded: longest side <= 45, then 25 x 45 (standard servo body is the ceiling)

fingers_g_per_mm.note: gripper_concept.py 8.8 g at L = 60, scaled with L

flange_max_mm.note: ear-to-ear span the housing's servo bay accepts (standard 40 x 20 servo ears are 54.5 mm [S Miuzei DS3218 and DS3235 drawings]); checked where flange_span_mm is published

hbridge_note.value: DRV8833-class driver sits with the MCU, 0 g on the gripper

hold_frac.note: 40 % case: hold <= 40 % of stall (R16), applied to EVERY actuator driven by a brushed DC motor (servos and gearmotors alike)

hold_frac_25.note: 25 % case: Pololu 'a general recommendation for brushed DC motor operation is 25% or less of the stall current', https://www.pololu.com/category/60/micro-metal-gearmotors; applied to EVERY brushed-DC-driven actuator (hobby servos contain brushed or coreless brushed DC motors)

housing_g.note: gripper_concept.py mass table (PLA, 60 % fill), via design_basis.py

k_sweep_N_mm.note: 0.42/0.76 = preliminary FEA-lane tip values (analysis/gripper/results/fea_stdout.txt, other lane); 0.88/1.63 = DESIGN-BASIS window

k_trap.note: trapezoid-profile time factor on the free-travel segment

kit_stall_tags.note: tag of params.json payload_scenarios.*.stall_Nm per kit

value.C001_5V: A: 1.618 N*m is the STS3215 6 V rating; at 5 V the stall is somewhat less (DESIGN-BASIS section 5), so every C001 5 V payload number here is OPTIMISTIC

lewis_sigma_per_Nm.note: MPa per N*m of mesh torque, b = 6 mm (design_basis.py Lewis table, DESIGN-BASIS section 2)

mu_nail_low.note: PLA nail on cotton, lower bound for the asymmetric-finger case (D7); fabric-fabric 0.28-0.30 [S cloth_and_camera.md 2.3]

overtravel_speed_max.note: deg/s ceiling while the FSR loop ramps force (firmware steps)

stage_eta.note: efficiency of one printed spur stage

stage_gear_fill.note: printed extra reduction stage, lightened gear, PETG 1.25 g/cm3

swing_rad.note: shoulder_lift swing for the dynamic check (min-jerk, ends at full extension)

vendor_hold_rule.note: part-specific published continuous rule: Pololu micro metal gearmotors 'a general recommendation for brushed DC motor operation is 25% or less of the stall current' https://www.pololu.com/category/60/micro-metal-gearmotors. The recommendation never applies a hold rule looser than the part's own vendor publishes

x_f_mm.note: pad x offset from pivot = m z/2 - gap/2 (m1 z24); 14.5 mm for m1.5 z20

allowable_hardware_mass_worst_pose.note: hardware = everything except cloth, camera and FSR wiring (fixed items at their own d); each value is the minimum over the joint ranges (optimised), the zero-pose value is kept for reference only

dc.rule: best base-weight score among DC gearmotor/worm + printed-stage configurations that pass every hard constraint AND hold under their vendor's published rule; if none, best score among those (vendor-consistent) whose ONLY failure is R19 with close <= 0.6 s (then R19 must be relaxed to 0.6 s)

recommendation.rule: pool = configurations that pass every hard constraint and also hold under their vendor's published hold rule (trade_vendor_consistent); primary = best-scoring in the pool that is in stock at its cited vendor (if none is in stock: best-scoring, flagged); backup = next best in the pool; DC branch = dc_pick rule
